findings_closed: Known-tag Native_declined results cannot turn EIO/EINVAL or inconsistent backend/phase/error combinations into suffix fallback. Both decode_native and direct typed run_native paths check decline consistency.
Copy.copyFile now passes requested-completed to the bounded fallback rather than requesting the original length after a reported prefix.
Buffered suffix output is flushed before the post-copy FD lseek/channel reconciliation. Computing that position before flush would otherwise rewind the cursor.
Windows source settles each reported pending IOCTL using its private manual-reset event before stack buffers/OVERLAPPED escape; the event close and original native error are accounted separately.
observations: Only explicit consistent scoped declines with no effect or a known reported prefix permit copying the suffix. Operational exceptions, malformed counts/statuses, native failures and indeterminate declines never acquire legacy errno fallback semantics.
Reported prefixes are bounded and counted once. Callback/cancellation exceptions stay outside native-error classification and propagate.
The additive native ABI preserves all eight scalar fields. C enum/ML tag mappings agree; negative or unknown raw tags/error representations reject before fallback.

Rooted OCaml parameters are retained; scalar/descriptor/handle values are copied before the no-pending runtime release. Native errno/GetLastError is saved before cursor checks/runtime reacquisition. No OCaml heap access occurs during release.
POSIX argument/access/alias/nonregular/append preflight is conservative. macOS returns an explicit platform/no-effect decline for a valid regular-file request.
Linux sendfile is attempted only after verified no-effect supported decline. Solaris partial-error count remains a terminal failure with a reported prefix.

Windows source uses the documented synchronous NtQueryObject basic layout/signature, exact returned-size check, original NTSTATUS bits and separately mapped Unix error; extent requests are exactly aligned lengths, not rounded up.

Borrowed descriptors/HANDLEs must remain valid/exclusive through settlement. An open descriptor does not make its content immutable. Existing source checks/leases/fingerprints/publication remain necessary.
